decisions.reason: The vertigo combination tablet sits close to the firm's core Rx/OTC offer, has its own web page, and has only been on the market for a year, so with the firm expanding and holding slack there is no performance shortfall to trigger dropping it.

The generic antidepressant capsule is distant from the established offer and faces price-driven, tender-dependent competition, which makes it the most likely candidate for problemistic search, but registration costs are already sunk and a single year of uncertain results gives an expanding firm with slack little reason to withdraw it yet.
The combination antihypertensive line with several models fits the firm's established cardiovascular-type portfolio and supports adherence, so it is likely to meet aspirations and be retained.

The bone and joint supplement only gets a website mention, suggesting low prominence, but it fits the strategy of pharmacy-exclusive self-care products that reduce reimbursement dependence and costs little to carry, so the firm keeps it.
